questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Spain because I already spoke a little spanish, which I wanted to improve.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Living in Barcelona is amazing and I can only recommend it! The weather is almost always nice and Barcelona has everything from mountains to beaches, clubs to museums and lots of nice restaurants and bars.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult. Due to IT-problems our schedules had not been published so most of us didn't know which courses we had been accepted to or when they took place. We had an online meeting the day classes began but the meeting was mostly about covid restrictions and presnetation of the school - not about the exchange program. At the meeting the administration was informed about the issue with the schedules.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: After the above mentioned online meeting, the administration decided to do the enrollment manually and scheduled a 15 minute meeting for all the exchange students during the following 2 weeks. The woman who helped me didn't speak english.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The first 2 weeks were very confusing because of the issue with the enrollment system.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is not impossible. I went to Barcelona 2 weeks before courses started to find housing. I joined facebook groups and reached out to people that way. I visited 2 places during the first 3 days and signed my contract with the second one in El Gótico. Doing it this way, I knew what to expect before signing anything. It's also possible to find housing beforehand. ESADE sends out a student handbook with ideas to websites where you can find housing but then you never know the quality of the apartment or the roomiesituation. It's also likely that you will have to pay a fee for using their services.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I prioritized to live in the city centre which is 35-40 minutes with public transportation to campus. I was really happy with this decision because the area where campus is is dead. However, living in the old part of Barcelona, the buildings are old so the standard is lower than in Denmark.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am happy that I found housing the way I did because beforehand I got to meet some of my roomies, who became my best friends there. So I can recommend to be crazy and go to Barcelona and live on a hostel until you find a nice housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was confusing. Some of the courses taught in english had a spanish title and the amount of ECTS listed on the course list differed from the actual course. The course describtion was only available for some of the courses so eventually I chose my courses based on the title and nothing else.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
In july we got an excel sheet with the time schedule of the courses
and access to course descriptions for most of the courses. From this material we should find courses that didn't overlap and register online. The first 2 weeks after arrival, it was possible to add and drop courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to email the program manager but she was not good at replying.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wanted but due to the IT-issue when we arrived, the people sceduled for the last individual meeting were not succesfull in getting all the courses they wanted because the courses had been filled already.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Breath and be patient. The pre approval from KU can be changed so don't stress about which courses you choose. I wish I had used the first 2 weeks trying out different courses and created a schedule without too long breaks and without evening classes. The master courses began later in september and continued for longer time so I would try to avoid them - also because the workload is bigger compared to the low amount of ECTS you get.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The amount of ECTS of each course seemed arbitrary compared to the workload.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Due to the fact that the courses are only 3-6 ECTS, you only get an introduction to the course. Thus, the level seems much lower than on KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very much like "seminarundervisning" on KU. Classes are mandatory and participation is included in the final grade. The exams were mostly closed book and handwritten which is far from what we're used to at KU but the questions were not that difficult and sometimes only multiple choice

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
3 ECTS Investment arbitration
3 ECTS Contract techniques
3 ECTS Competition Law
3 ECTS Intellectual Proporty, Patents and Trademark

4 ECTS International Human Rights Protection

5 ECTS Comparative Law
5 ECTS World Trade Law
5 ECTS International Sales Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I think comparative law was really interesting because I got to see how different legal systems work. 

Intellectual proporty, patents and trademark was really an interesting course as well if you haven't had intellectual proporty before.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I had any. I knew that I didn't want to think about money when I was on exchange so I went on trips, to FC Barcelona matches, to the cinema and to restaurants.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and beer were extremely cheap. Going to restaurants was in generel a bit cheaper than Denmark but not cheap cheap. Taxis were also more affordable. Apartments/rooms were more or less the same price as Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was possible to join a "body"-system before we went to Barcelona. The "body"-system was an international student organization with ESADE students organizing different events for exchange students. Even though I didn't join the "body"-system, I gained access to the whats-app group and got all the information about events. There was a beachvolleytournament, a hike to the bunkers, a hike on Montjuic and a student party in a club.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above the international student organization organized different events. Moreover ESADE has a volleyballteam, which you can find on instagram and here you find information about try-outs - it's in the beginning of the semester, so I was too late.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recomment to explore the city. Everything is possible! I went bouldering, to beachvolley and social dancing. It's also possible to join a fitness or train at the beach in an outdoor "gym".

There is an app called "meetup" where you can find gatherings with other expats.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on Erasmus trips! Find Erasmus on instagram where they have a link to their website and here you can join day trips out of Barcelona ex. Montserrat, Andorra, Mont Rebei, Valencia, Costa Brava, Girona etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It wasn't that difficult. It was fun to observe how different it was from Denmark but not difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are more local students in the master courses but in generel the exchange students didn't socialize with the local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The laid back culture was a bit difficult to adjust to. We often said "well it's Barcelona" when the bus didn't come, when the 5 minute break was 15 minutes and when the power in the apartment went off. In the beginning I always forgot that shops and supermarkets were closed on sundays and holidays but in the end I didn't  notice.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked how multicultural Barcelina was both regarding food and people. And I also liked that the day often didn't start until 10 am.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be patient and openminded. Everything will work out in the end so stressing out about courses and exam dates is wasted energy. 

Students going on exchange are people who want to meet people, so no worries about finding friends - they will be there. Join Erasmus groups on Facebook to get information about Erasmus events where you can meet other Erasmus students. 

It's okay not to do something everyday because you're not on vacation, you're living in Barcelona. A day in bed can be wisely spent.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be attentive and ask when you're in doubt because you are not getting the information from other sources. If you speak spanish it's a huge advantage but it's possible to go to Barcelona without.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I meet so many different people from different cultures which expanded my view of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: ESADE administration gave me grey hair. The whole situation in the beginning with the courses really challenged my patience. The dates for the exams were also constantly changing until mid November so it was difficult to book a flight home for christmas.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was worth all the challenges.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
